sources.note: A survey organizing mechanistic findings about reasoning models into training dynamics, reasoning mechanisms and unintended behaviours, and arguing the field needs a unified theoretical framework.
sources.title: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Large Reasoning Models: A Survey of Training, Inference, and Failures

sources.note: A survey reorganizing mechanistic interpretability from observation into a Locate-Steer-Improve intervention pipeline, categorized by the interpretable object being acted on.
sources.title: Locate, Steer, and Improve: A Practical Survey of Actionable Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models

result.definition: A review paper rather than a technique applied to models; it appears as an entity here because two archived sources are surveys of the same field and named it as their method. The two organize mechanistic interpretability incompatibly: one by object of study — training dynamics, reasoning mechanisms, unintended behaviours — and the other by intervention, as a Locate, Steer and Improve pipeline categorized by the interpretable object acted on. Both name the same gap, that the field's findings are not yet actionable or auditable. Two irreconcilable taxonomies of one area arriving together is itself a description of the field's state.
